title: Challenges in Guardrailing Large Language Models for Science

bias_targets.methodology: The paper does not empirically measure this bias, but proposes a theoretical taxonomic framework and implementation strategies (white-box, black-box, and gray-box guardrails) to evaluate and mitigate the over-representation of certain hypotheses and flawed conclusions in scientific LLM applications.

The paper identifies institutional bias as a critical vulnerability in the scientific domain and proposes theoretical guardrailing mechanisms to ensure research quality, without conducting empirical measurements.

The paper discusses evaluating and mitigating positivity bias (the tendency of LLMs to provide overly optimistic responses that underestimate risks) through knowledge contextualization and adaptive reasoning, though no empirical experiments are performed.
